question: What is the chemical name for the powder used to make Plaster of Paris?
explanation: Plaster of Paris is produced by heating gypsum to create calcium sulfate hemihydrate powder. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why does a curing Plaster of Paris cast feel warm to the touch?

options.A: Body heat is trapped inside the wet cotton padding
options.B: Electric warmers are used to speed up drying
options.C: Friction from bandage wrapping creates thermal energy
options.D: An exothermic hydration reaction releases heat

explanation: Mixing the powder with water causes a chemical reaction that naturally produces heat as it hardens. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h1)

question: The primary clinical purpose of applying a Plaster of Paris cast is what?

options.A: Immobilize fractured bones to promote healing
options.B: Increase local blood circulation in limbs
options.C: Prevent muscle hypertrophy during bed rest
options.D: Deliver topical antibiotics to open wounds

explanation: Casts hold broken bone ends steady to allow proper alignment and callus formation. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h2)

question: A child with clubfoot is brought to the clinic for serial casting. What is the main goal?

options.A: Protect the skin from insect bites
options.D: Keep the infant from crawling early

explanation: Serial casting uses the rigid support of POP to gradually stretch tight soft tissues and correct skeletal malformations. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the function of the stockinette placed before the plaster roll?

options.A: Protect the skin from friction and irritation
options.B: Absorb excess heat generated by the water
options.C: Add structural weight and strength to the limb
options.D: Speed up the drying time of the outer cast

explanation: The stockinette acts as a soft barrier between the rough plaster material and the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why should a nurse use tepid water instead of hot water for soaking POP bandages?

options.A: Cold water makes the plaster completely dissolve into liquid
options.B: Tepid water is required to activate the chemical coloring agents
options.C: Hot water causes the plaster to set too fast and generates excess heat
options.D: Hot water prevents the plaster from ever hardening at all

explanation: Water temperature dictates setting speed; excessively hot water causes rapid hardening and risks burning the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h3)

question: How should a nurse submerge a Plaster of Paris bandage into the water basin?

options.A: Soak it overnight in a sealed plastic container
options.B: Hold it vertically under a running tap for seconds
options.C: Immerse it horizontally until bubbling ceases
options.D: Boil the roll in water before wrapping the limb

explanation: Horizontal immersion allows water to penetrate the core evenly, indicated by the cessation of air bubbles. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why must the operator avoid using fingertips to mold a fresh wet cast?

options.A: Indentations can press into the skin and cause pressure sores
options.B: Pressure from fingertips makes the cast crack in half
options.C: Natural oils on fingers dissolve the wet plaster material
options.D: Fingerprints permanently ruin the shiny outer finish

explanation: Using the palms of the hands instead of fingertips prevents localized pressure points from forming inside the hardening cast. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h4)

question: What are the key clinical indicators checked during a neurovascular assessment of a casted limb?

options.A: Muscle tone, pupil reaction, reflexes, posture
options.D: Skin turgor, bowel sounds, urine output, jaundice

explanation: These five clinical signs help nurses detect early compartment syndrome or circulation blockage. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h5)

question: How should a fresh wet Plaster of Paris cast be supported while drying on a bed?

options.A: Wrapped tightly with heavy thermal blankets
options.B: On flat palm pillows to prevent flat spots
options.C: Directly on the hard wooden mattress frame
options.D: Suspended vertically by a single narrow cord

explanation: Resting a wet cast on hard edges deforms the shape, while using palms distributes weight evenly. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the hallmark symptom of compartment syndrome in a patient with a new cast?

options.A: Itching skin underneath the cotton stockinette padding
options.B: Severe pain that does not respond to prescribed analgesics
options.C: A slight increase in overall body core temperature
options.D: Excessive sweating on the toes of the affected leg

explanation: Unrelenting, disproportionate pain that worsens with passive stretching of the fingers or toes is a classic warning sign of compartment syndrome. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized complication of prolonged Plaster of Paris immobilization?

options.A: Joint stiffness and reduced range of motion

explanation: Casts immobilize limbs and cause muscle wasting or stiffness, but they do not cause bones to rapidly grow longer. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h6)

question: What instruction should a nurse give a patient regarding an itchy skin sensation inside their cast?

options.A: Apply medicated oils directly onto the plaster
options.B: Use a knitting needle gently to reach the spot
options.C: Never insert objects into the cast to scratch
options.D: Pour cool water down the opening to soothe skin

explanation: Inserting foreign items can break the skin barrier, causing hidden wounds and severe deep tissue infections. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why is limb elevation recommended during the first two days after cast application?

options.A: It helps reduce and prevent dependent swelling
options.B: It allows the underlying bone to knit together faster
options.C: It prevents dust from settling on the wet surface
options.D: It accelerates the chemical drying of the plaster

explanation: Keeping the limb elevated above heart level promotes venous return and controls post-injury edema. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h7)

question: How does an electric cast cutter blade move to prevent cutting the patient's skin?

options.A: It oscillates back and forth rapidly
options.B: It generates a high-frequency laser beam
options.C: It rotates in a continuous circular motion
options.D: It melts the plaster using hot air streams

explanation: The oscillating motion cuts rigid plaster easily while safe against yielding soft tissues like skin. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h8)

question: What is a normal finding when a patient's limb is first freed from a long-term cast?

options.A: Complete restoration of full muscle strength immediately
options.B: Dry, scaly skin and temporary muscle weakness
options.C: Excessive elongation of the newly healed bone
options.D: Bright red skin rashes caused by chemical burns

explanation: Accumulated dead skin cells and disuse atrophy are expected after weeks of confinement inside a rigid cast. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h8)
